explanation: Arrested breech delivery with extended arms above the head is managed by Lovset manoeuvre (rotating the body through 180 degrees) to bring down the arms; Pinard is for extended legs and Burns-Marshall, Piper's forceps and Mauriceau-Smellie-Veit are for the head.
key_note: Source option C read 'Pinard manoeuvre'; the intended answer is the manoeuvre for extended arms (Lovset), so the option was corrected.

stem: A non-booked primigravida admitted in labour. On examination there is malpresentation of fetus. She insists for vaginal delivery. You will counsel her that mode of delivery will be decided after initial evaluation because safe vaginal delivery can be anticipated in:
explanation: Of the malpresentations given, mentoanterior face presentation can deliver vaginally; shoulder, brow, cord presentation and footling breech cannot.

stem: You attend a patient in labour ward. Duty nurse informs you that patient is in active phase of labour. On vaginal examination cervical os is 5cm, membranes are absent, presenting part is face with chin directed anteriorly. CTG is reactive. Your plan for this patient will be

options.E: Give epidural and watch for progress

explanation: Face with the chin anterior and a reactive CTG: allow labour to progress with careful monitoring; caesarean only if mentoposterior or no progress.
key_note: Paper key marked E (Give epidural and watch for progress); the essential step is watching progress.

stem: A 32 year old G3P2 is in labour at 37 weeks. She is 7 cm dilated for last 3 hours. Bregma is felt anteriorly. What is measurement of presenting part?
explanation: The mentovertical diameter of a brow presentation is about 13 cm, the largest presenting diameter, and it obstructs vaginal delivery.
key_note: Stem is unclear (bregma felt anteriorly); the paper key for brow (13 cm) is kept.

stem: A G6P5 presents in labour ward at 39 weeks of gestation. On abdominal examination lie of baby is transverse with head in left lumber region. On ultrasound fetal biometry is according to gestation but AFI is 28 cm. On vaginal examination cervical os is 8 cm with intact membranes and presenting part is not felt vaginally. Your plan of management in this case will be

options.A: Perform controlled ARM and watch for progress
options.B: Perform ARM and start oxytocin infusion
options.C: Start oxytocin infusion and maintain partogram
options.E: Hydrate the patient and watch for progress

explanation: Transverse lie with polyhydramnios in labour: ARM risks cord and arm prolapse, so caesarean section is needed.

stem: You are delivering a G3 P2 with dichorionic diamniotic twins. First twin delivers. Second is transverse. Fetal heart is 140/min with type 1 deceleration. Membranes rupture and liquor has a tinge of meconium. What should be your line of management?

options.C: Move to OT for Category I Caesarean section

explanation: Second twin transverse with ruptured membranes and meconium: ECV is hard after membrane rupture, so IPV with breech extraction is quick.
key_note: Paper keys marked both ECV and IPV; with ruptured membranes IPV is preferred.

stem: 32 year old G3P2 at 36 weeks presented in labour room,she has DCDA twins.Twin 1 has delivered cephalic,twin 2 is high in the pelvis with transverse lie and back upward,membrans are intect.there are decelerations on CTG.what you will do for delivery of 2nd twin?
explanation: Second twin transverse with decelerations needs rapid delivery: IPV with breech extraction by a skilled operator.

stem: A 28 years old women G3 P2+0 at 38+4 weeks gestation with twin pregnancy is admitted to the labour room having mild to moderate regular uterine contraction. On examination Os 5cm dilated Her membrane are intact both twins are cephalic Two hours after her initial vaginal EX. Os is 5.5cm What would be your next plan of management.
explanation: Twin labour with slow progress (0.5 cm in 2 hours), intact membranes and cephalic twins: ARM to augment progress.

stem: A 32-year-old multiparous woman at 39 weeks gestation is in active labour. Her partogram shows that the cervical dilatation curve has reached the action line. She has been on oxytocin infusion for 4 hours with good contractions (4-5 in 10 minutes, each lasting 45 seconds). Fetal heart rate is 170 bpm, cervix is 6 cm dilated and the liquor is thick meconium stained. What is the most appropriate management at this stage?

options.A: Continue oxytocin and observe for 1 more hour
options.C: Give tocolytic and reassess fetal condition

explanation: Fetal tachycardia of 170 bpm with thick meconium and failure to progress despite 4 hours of oxytocin (action line crossed) indicates fetal compromise and failed augmentation: immediate caesarean section.

stem: A 30-year-old woman, G3P2, is admitted to the labor ward with a diagnosis of obstructed labor. The fetal head is engaged at +1 station, but there has been no progress in the descent for 3 hours despite adequate contractions and caput 3+. The cervix is fully dilated, and the patient is experiencing significant fetal distress with a non-reassuring heart rate pattern. Your management in this case will be

options.A: Perform a trial of vacuum-assisted delivery
options.B: Administer tocolytics to relax the uterus
options.D: Increase the dose of oxytocin to augment labor
options.E: Attempt manual rotation of the fetus

explanation: Obstructed labour with caput 3+ and a non-reassuring fetal heart rate: emergency caesarean. Vacuum, more oxytocin or tocolysis are unsafe or ineffective.

stem: A 28-year-old G2P1 attends antenatal clinic at 41 weeks. SFH is 36 cm, longitudinal lie, cephalic, 2/5 palpable, fetal heart present. On vaginal examination she is 4 cm dilated, cervical length is 0.5 cm, the head is at -1 and the cervix is soft and anterior. Which is the most suitable medication for induction or augmentation of labour?
explanation: With a favourable cervix (4 cm, soft, effaced, low station) oxytocin, after amniotomy, is used. Prostaglandins and misoprostol are for ripening an unfavourable cervix.
key_note: Two papers marked A (prostaglandin), one noting 'to initiate contractions'; for a favourable cervix oxytocin is correct.

stem: A 32-year-old G3P2 in labour at 37 weeks with twins has a cephalic first twin and a footling breech second twin. After the first twin is delivered vaginally, what is the best option for the second twin?

options.B: Rupture of membranes and commence syntocinon

explanation: With a stable second twin, ECV (or breech extraction) allows vaginal delivery; waiting for long or caesarean are not routine.
key_note: Breech extraction is an equally accepted option; paper key D retained.

stem: You have just delivered a 2.5 kg infant at 39 weeks from a twin pregnancy. A second sac is bulging through a fully dilated cervix, a small part is presenting, and the fetal heart is 60 beats per minute. What is the most appropriate procedure?
explanation: With a fully dilated cervix, intact membranes and fetal bradycardia, internal podalic version with breech extraction is the quickest way to deliver the second twin.
key_note: Paper key marked D (caesarean); the classical teaching answer is B for an emergency second twin with bradycardia.

stem: Interlocking twins is associated with which of the following presentations?
explanation: Interlocking occurs when the chin of the first (breech) twin locks with the chin of the second (cephalic) twin; it is a rare complication of breech-cephalic presentation.

stem: A 25-year-old primigravida in labour at 34 weeks has fundal height appropriate for gestation and a reactive CTG. On vaginal examination she is 6 cm dilated and fully effaced, with the fetal nose and mouth palpable and the chin pointing towards the maternal left hip. This is an example of:
explanation: Palpable nose, mouth and chin indicates a face presentation (extended head); chin to the left hip is a mento-lateral position.
